newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-WARNE IN EARLY BREAK BUT LARA STILL THERE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-WARNE IN EARLY BREAK BUT LARA STILL THERE.

text.p: Wrist spinner Shane Warne made a crucial breakthrough after Australia set West Indies a daunting victory target of 420 in the first test on Monday.
But there were ominous signs late in the day that West Indies number three Brian Lara could yet ruin Mark Taylor's calculations, although history still favours an Australia victory.
At close of play on the fourth day at the Gabba, West Indies were 89 for one in 29 overs, still needing another 331 runs to win from a minimum of 90 overs after an absorbing day.
Warne dismissed opener Robert Samuels for 29 at the end of an extraordinary over that also featured one six, two fours and a dropped catch.
Lara, the world record holder for the highest score in test and first-class cricket, stroked five boundaries in a late flourish to remain unbeaten on 29 at the close.
The West Indies vice-captain played with poise and aggression, appearing untroubled in partnership with opener Sherwin Campbell, who finished on 28 not out.
If West Indies reach their target of 420 it will be the highest winning second innings total in the history of the game.

Warne, playing in his first test since undergoing surgery on the ring finger of his bowling hand in May, found the inside edge of Samuels's bat, deflecting the ball on to wicketkeeper Ian Healy's pads.
The ball looped gently to Taylor at first slip for a simple catch to give Warne his third wicket for the match.

Earlier in the over, Samuels smashed a six over deep square leg, hit one four and was then dropped on the boundary by pace bowler Paul Reiffel, who allowed the ball to roll over the boundary rope for another four.
Resuming on eight for no wicket, Australia reached 217 for six in 65 overs before captain Taylor declared the innings just after tea.
Healy, who scored an unbeaten 161 in the first innings, contributed a brisk 45 not out in just 50 balls as Australia chased quick runs after lunch. Mark Waugh was top scorer with 57.
Australia suffered a blow earlier in the day when all-rounder Steve Waugh was unable to bat after sustaining a groin injury while bowling on Sunday.
Waugh, who did not take the field for West Indies second innings, said he will miss the second test, starting in Sydney on Friday.
But he believes Australia still hold the advantage in Brisbane.
"I would rather be in our position right not rather than West Indies'. I think the pitch will offer us more help on the final day," Waugh told reporters.
